name: read_budget.READ_SECONDS
why: of the search's 3 minutes (time_budget.part): no new site after this; the AI steps get the time after the cut

name: read_budget.READ_FLOOR
why: sites read whatever the read's clock says, before the cut: the best ones of every search

name: read_budget.READ_GRACE
why: a site already open may take this long past the read's time; then it is left for the next run, not waited for

name: read_budget.BETWEEN_S
why: how often a read's loop looks at the rounds its open boards ended meanwhile (as_done between): a grain, never a deadline

name: boards.SHARE_S
why: Of the press's 180 s (src/time_budget.py PLANNED, scaled to the run's budget): the job boards' step ends here and the search gets the rest (owner's 06:21 press, 26 Oct 2026: this step took 177 s of 269 with no clock; earlier presses 52-56 s). Tests: tests/unit/sources/test_three_minutes.py.

name: boards_first.WEB_WAIT
why: seconds the run waits for its web search before any employer site (the pilot search's answered at 37 s on the plan)

name: eures.SECONDS
why: with no run deadline, a read stops asking for more pages this long after its first page may go

name: eures.LAST_PAGE
why: seconds a page asked just before the stop time still gets

name: eures.MOST
why: per read: a read returned 173-234 jobs before areas (#2918), so the AI steps after it keep their load

name: eures.KEEP
why: per area: enough near home, the next place gets its turn

name: national.PAGES
why: pages of a national employment service read per role word and place (100 ads a page in Sweden's feed): the best matches first, the rest waits for another search

name: national.MOST
why: ads of a national employment service kept per read, so the titles' AI after it keeps its load (Stockholm, customer support: 45 ads within 30 km for one word, 12 Nov 2026)

name: first_jobs.SLICE
why: feeds read first, before the full read, so a first Find jobs run puts its first jobs on screen early

name: first_jobs.FIRST_JOBS
why: jobs scored first, at once

name: first_jobs.MAX_FIRST
why: scored at most in the slice while none fits FIT+ yet: the full search would score these same best-ranked jobs anyway

name: first_jobs.SLICE_BOARDS
why: read at once (owner, 19 Oct 2026: music's only paying board, XING, was 7th of the proposal and read at 351 s; up to board_yield.MAX_UNTRIED, the untried boards one read takes); a board that refuses is replaced by the next proposed one, once

name: title_triage.BATCH
why: ~30 s a batch through Claude Code (100 took ~2 min): a 3-minute search can stop between them

name: title_triage.BATCH_THINKING
why: titles in one call when the step thinks before it answers (the provider says so: Claude Code's structured answer, two turns, src/ai/providers/claude_code.py THINK_FIRST): that fixed cost is paid once a call, so a bigger batch sorts more titles a second. gp, 12 Nov 2026, 40 calls on Haiku 5.5: 30 titles 7.2 s (4.2 titles a second), 60 titles 8.6 s (7.0 a second), right titles kept 94% at both, unrelated kept 1.0 vs 0.9 per 30 (one call of 60 kept 5); 90 kept 84% of the right ones. Cost: a stop between batches leaves up to 60 titles, the furthest, for the next search; a fresh install's default title_rounds pace (10 s a round) under-guesses a thinking round about 2x until its first refresh measures its own. Codex and the in-house AI answer in one turn and keep BATCH until measured.

name: title_triage.MAX_NEW
why: titles asked about in one run at most, of each kind: your own places' titles and the others (a first run on a big list is spread over the next ones)

name: app.SEARCH_BUDGET_S
why: one deadline for the whole Find jobs run (owner, 26 Oct 2026: "A find jobs session should take at most 3min")

name: app.SCOUT_SHARE_S
why: the employer finder's seconds at the press's end, when it is due

name: app.STOP_MARGIN_S
why: Why (27 Oct 2026, Gitar on #2285): the SIGTERM handler writes the row (a Notion call) and may wait EXIT_GRACE_S (3 s); the stop starts this long before 180 s so the step is gone by the press's end.

name: app.STEP_MIN_S
why: fewer seconds left: the step waits for the next search (an engine step needs a few to start)
